title: CLAUDE.md
text: Use UK English spelling throughout (e.g. “serialise”, “centralise”, “behaviour”, “colour”, “summarise”) Follow existing code style: snake_case functions variables Use cli error handling (codeminer_abort, codeminer_warn, codeminer_inform) Use glue::glue_sql() parameterised SQL queries Use dplyr / dbplyr lazy table operations possible Prefer tidyverse packages already Imports (dplyr, purrr, stringr, tidyr, tibble) base R equivalents read clearly — e.g. purrr::map() rather loop rows, stringr::str_sub() rather substr(). Don’t force tidyverse base genuinely simpler (vectorised arithmetic, predicates, etc.) Avoid superseded dplyr verbs (e.g. transmute()); use current equivalents (mutate() + select())

title: Introduction to codeminer
text: multiple versions lookup, mapping, relationship table available, codeminer resolves "latest" automatically. first time query function resolves "latest" given code type, resolved version cached remainder session. avoids repeated informational messages ensures consistent version usage across workflow. can override current session codeminer_set_version(): Pins affect default "latest" resolution. Explicit version arguments always take precedence: clear version selections return automatic "latest" resolution: can also clear versions selectively code type: codeminer_status() shows active versions alongside connection info.
code: # Pin lookup and relationship versions for a code type codeminer_set_version(   lookup       = c("ICD-10" = "UKB v4"),   relationship = c("ICD-10" = "UKB v4") )  # Pin a mapping version (use "from > to" format for the key) codeminer_set_version(   mapping = c("Read v3 > ICD-10" = "UKB v4") ) # This uses the pinned version for ICD-10: CODES("E10", type = "ICD-10") #> <codeminer_codelist>: 1 code #> Code type: "ICD-10" #>  #> # A tibble: 1 × 3 #>   code  description              code_type #>   <chr> <chr>                    <chr>     #> 1 E10   Type 1 diabetes mellitus ICD-10  # This ignores the pin and uses "UKB v4" directly: CODES("E10", type = "ICD-10", lookup_version = "UKB v4") #> <codeminer_codelist>: 1 code #> Code type: "ICD-10" #>  #> # A tibble: 1 × 3 #>   code  description              code_type #>   <chr> <chr>                    <chr>     #> 1 E10   Type 1 diabetes mellitus ICD-10 codeminer_clear_versions() # Clear only the ICD-10 lookup version codeminer_clear_versions(lookup = "ICD-10")  # Clear lookup and relationship for SNOMED CT codeminer_clear_versions(   lookup = "SNOMED CT",   relationship = "SNOMED CT" )

title: Introduction to codeminer
text: query functions accept col_filters parameter three options: "default" (default): apply filters session pin metadata defaults NULL: filtering — return rows regardless column values named list: apply explicit filters call
code: # Default: only active concepts (from metadata defaults) CODES("all", type = "SNOMED CT")  # Override: return all rows including inactive CODES("all", type = "SNOMED CT", col_filters = NULL)  # Custom: only inactive concepts CODES("all", type = "SNOMED CT", col_filters = list(active_concept = c("0")))

title: Introduction to codeminer
text: important design point: table type independent col_filters. matters MAP(), touches two table types: mapping table (e.g., Read v3 → ICD-10) may filters like mapping_status target lookup table (e.g., ICD-10) may filters like active_concept call MAP(col_filters = ...), controls mapping table. target lookup table uses default filters looking descriptions. intentional — two tables different filterable columns different semantics. override filters target lookup well, use session pinning:
code: # Pin lookup filters for SNOMED CT codeminer_set_col_filters(   lookup = list("SNOMED CT" = list(active_concept = c("0", "1"))) )  # Now MAP() will use the pinned lookup filters for the target table MAP("24700007", from = "SNOMED CT", to = "ICD-10")

title: Introduction to codeminer
text: Like version pinning, can pin col_filters entire session:
code: # Pin: include inactive SNOMED concepts codeminer_set_col_filters(   lookup = list("SNOMED CT" = list(active_concept = c("0", "1"))) )  # Clear all filter pins codeminer_clear_col_filters()

title: Temporarily override column filters — with_col_filters
text: Sets column filter pins duration supplied code block, restores previous state. useful need different filters group calls without permanently changing session state.

title: Temporarily override column filters — with_col_filters
code: with_col_filters(code, lookup = NULL, relationship = NULL, mapping = NULL)

title: Temporarily override column filters — with_col_filters
text: code Code execute temporary filters. lookup Named list column filters lookup tables, keyed code type. value named list column_name = c(values) pairs. E.g. list("SNOMED CT" = list(active_concept = c("1"))). relationship Named list column filters relationship tables, keyed code type. mapping Named list column filters mapping tables, keyed "> " pairs. E.g. list("Read 3 > ICD-10" = list(mapping_status = c("E", "G"))).

text: result evaluating code.

title: Set code type context — with_type
text: with_type() temporarily sets active code type query functions inside code use without needing explicit type = argument. Convenience wrappers (icd10(), sct(), etc.) call with_type() supported code type.

title: Set code type context — with_type
code: with_type(type, code)  icd10(code)  icd9(code)  read3(code)  read2(code)  sct(code)  opcs4(code)  phecode(code)  read2_drugs(code)  bnf(code)  dmd(code)  data_coding_3(code)  data_coding_4(code)  data_coding_5(code)  data_coding_6(code)

title: Set code type context — with_type
text: type string naming code type (e.g. "ICD-10", "SNOMED CT"). corresponds type argument accepted query functions CODES(), CHILDREN(), MAP(). code expression evaluate within code type context.

title: Set code type context — with_type
text: result evaluating code.
